title: Importing or exporting goods
description: Your answers describe the goods you're bringing into or sending out of Australia and how they will travel. Declarations, permits and registrations are identified later from sourced rules; check anything you're unsure of with a licensed customs broker.

questions.label: Are you importing, exporting or both?
Describe the goods in a few words
questions.help_text: For example: espresso machines from Italy, or frozen prawns to Japan.

questions.label: Which of these describe the goods?
questions.help_text: Pick every one that fits. Choose "General goods" if none of the others do.

options.label: General goods (clothing, homewares, toys, furniture and the like)
Plants, seeds, bulbs, cut flowers or plant products
Live animals, meat, dairy, eggs, fish or other animal products
Cars, motorbikes, trailers or other road vehicles
Machinery, metal goods, stone, ceramics or glass
Air conditioners, fridges or other equipment with refrigerant gas
Chemicals, or products with them such as cosmetics, soap, paint or glue
Wildlife, or products from protected plants or animals
Military goods, or technology with military uses (for example drones, encryption or advanced electronics)

questions.label: What is the value of a typical shipment you will import?
questions.help_text: The customs value of the goods in one consignment, in Australian dollars.

options.label: By sea, in a shipping container
By sea, as break bulk, on a flat rack or in an open-top container

questions.label: Are the goods made in, or shipped from or through, one of the countries listed below?
questions.help_text: Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czechia, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Switzerland, Türkiye, Ukraine, the United States or Uzbekistan.

questions.label: Will any shipments leave between 1 September and 30 April?
Will you lodge import declarations yourself, rather than using a customs broker?
Will any one shipment hold more than five pieces of this equipment, or weigh 10 kg or more in total?
Is the electrical equipment mains powered and made or sold for household, personal or similar use?
questions.help_text: Rated above 50 volts AC. For example kettles, heaters, chargers, power tools or lights. Large industrial equipment is usually not included.

questions.label: What is the value of a typical shipment you will export?
questions.help_text: The value of the goods in one consignment, in Australian dollars.

questions.label: Does the business have an ABN?
Is the business registered for GST?
Which state or territory is the business based in?
